newsitem.title: USA: White House slams IRA for violent acts.
newsitem.headline: White House slams IRA for violent acts.

text.p: The White House condemned the Irish Republican Army on Wednesday for two violent acts in recent days, saying it threatened to wreck progress toward peace in Northern Ireland.

"Yesterday in Northern Ireland, the IRA claimed responsibility for shots that were fired at a vehicle carrying British troops. Thankfully there were no injuries," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said in a written statement.
McCurry said the Clinton administration was "deeply concerned" about this incident as well as the abandoning of a van full of explosives in Belfast last week, an action also claimed by the IRA.
"Violence can only derail the progress that has been made in recent weeks," McCurry said, referring to overtures made by the new Labour government of British Prime Minister Tony Blair.

He said the administration "joins the many Americans who have worked for a resolution of this conflict in calling for an immediate unequivocal end to violence, which threatens to wreck the prospects for meaningful, inclusive negotiations on the future of Northern Ireland."
